qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Global fast-food franchisor with iconic brand intangibles (Tim Hortons, Burger King, Popeyes, Firehouse Subs) across 31,000+ units. The ~98% franchised model captures menu price inflation directly via percentage-of-sales royalties. Tangible operating ROIC exceeds 50%, though GAAP ROIC is ~9-11% due to $17.5B in acquisition goodwill. Primary erosion threats: franchisee margin squeeze from labor/food costs, market share losses to McDonald's, and aggressive discounting.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (REJECT). While Restaurant Brands International operates an asset-light, highly cash-generative fast-food franchise model (>100% FCF conversion) with entrenched everyday consumer habits (Tim Hortons morning coffee ritual, Burger King value dining), it structurally fails the Munger peace-of-mind fortress balance sheet standard. Legacy debt from 3G Capital's debt-financed acquisitions leaves QSR burdened with $15.7B in total debt and $14.5B in net debt against $776M-$1,021M of GAAP net income (14.3x to 18.7x Net Debt/NI, far exceeding the <=4.0x ceiling; 10.0x Net Debt/FCF). EBIT interest coverage is persistently depressed at 3.4x to 4.2x (4-year median ~3.86x), failing the >5.0x through-the-cycle requirement. With annual dividends ($1.1B) consuming ~75% of FCF, the company cannot organically retire debt and remains perpetually reliant on debt market refinancing ('kindness of strangers').
qualitative.evidence: Asset-light global restaurant franchisor (~98% franchised across 31,000+ units in 100+ countries). Free cash flow conversion is strong at >100% of GAAP Net Income ($1.45B FCF vs $776M Net Income in FY2025; $1.30B FCF vs $1.02B Net Income in FY2024) with low maintenance capex ($200-265M on $8.4-9.4B revenue). Tangible Operating ROIC is >50%, but reported GAAP ROIC is mediocre at 8.8% to 11.3% (5Y median ~9.7%) due to $17.5B in capitalized acquisition goodwill and brand intangibles. Structural Gate 6 failure is absolute: Total debt is $15.70B, Net debt is $14.54B, and Stockholders' Equity is $3.63B against negative tangible equity (-$13.86B). Net Debt to Net Income stands at 18.7x in FY2025 (14.3x in FY2024; 11.2x in FY2023; 13.2x in FY2022) and Net Debt to FCF is 10.0x, massively violating the 4.0-year Owner Earnings ceiling. EBIT interest coverage has failed the 5.0x threshold in every year of the cycle (FY2022: 3.67x, FY2023: 3.44x, FY2024: 4.06x, FY2025: 4.23x; 4-year median 3.86x). Dividends of $1.1B annually consume almost all free cash flow, leaving zero organic capacity for debt amortization.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
